reason: The 320-byte scratch stride is a bounded, distinct test: its 163,840-byte allocation covers all 512 slices and both row halves, though it exceeds the supplied 128 KiB P-core L1D and the cache mapping benefit is unknown. Fused transpose-and-consume could remove scratch traffic, but the proposal lacks a verified legal instruction path that preserves K order. The store-order change has low correctness risk and little evidence of benefit. n512_fast_path and assembly_audit specify the same TB descriptor and 1 MiB A transpose, so treat them as aliases and abstain if one has already been tested; TB packing savings do not establish net gain. The remaining descriptor options add timed conversions: panel_packing converts all of B, while TA and TT convert both inputs, making their cost and benefit uncertain. No noisy score supports a causal claim for any proposal.
